title: Count the Number of Good Subarrays
summary: Determine the count of subarrays in an integer array where at least k pairs of identical elements exist at different indices.
statement: Determine the count of subarrays in an integer array where at least k pairs of identical elements exist at different indices.
constraints: A pair consists of two different indices in a subarray holding equal values.
A subarray is good when it contains at least k such unordered pairs.
Return the number of good contiguous subarrays.
hints: Adding a value creates one new pair with every equal value already in the window.
Once a window has at least k pairs, every extension to its right is also good.
Count all those extensions, remove the left value, and continue while the window remains good.
Each good subarray is counted when its left endpoint is removed from the first qualifying window ending at or before its right endpoint.
editorial: Each good subarray is counted when its left endpoint is removed from the first qualifying window ending at or before its right endpoint.

tests.explanation: All five elements form exactly ten equal-value pairs, so only the full array qualifies.
Exactly four subarrays accumulate at least two matching pairs.
